correctness.rationale: For any odd q>1, the root congruence \(x^2\equiv2q-1\pmod{4q}\) reduces to \(x^2\equiv-1\pmod q\) with an odd lift; Hensel and CRT give exactly \(2^{\omega(q)+1}\) root generators, yielding \(2^{\omega(q)}\) cyclic order-four subgroups. For a root x, \(x^3\equiv2q-x\pmod{4q}\) gives subgroup sum \(4q\) below the halfway point, \(8q\) above. Translation \(x\mapsto x+2q\) is well defined on generators, involutory, fixed-point-free, and swaps the two sums, proving the equal multiplicities and absence of −1. The verification script tests 999 odd q up to 1999 but is not used for the universal proof.

Full-coset half-interval balance would imply the subgroup has two elements in each half, but it does not by itself supply the exact integer first moment; conversely the present centered subgroups are eventually not globally coset-balanced by Pomerance–Ulmer Theorem 3.1.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural local-involution fiber in the subgroup-centering problem and provides a uniform existence test, exact \(2^{\omega(q)}\) count, and a nontrivial equal split of two distinct first-moment values for every allowable odd composite q. It exhibits centered order-four subgroups not containing −1 and distinguishes centered first moments from global coset balance; these are motivated arithmetic invariants, not an arbitrary finite sample or a restatement of root counting.
